title: Stochastic predator-prey compartment model with cyclic and non-cyclic transition pathways and mortality
summary: We study variants of a stochastic SEIRS-SEID compartmental model incorporating presymptomatic infectiousness and disease-related mortality, with independent compartmental sojourn times drawn from arbitrary distributions, in particular Weibull distributions. We consider a large population of agents that occupy the states (compartments) S (susceptible to infection), E (exposed: infected but asymptomatic during the latency period and already infectious, including diseases with presymptomatic infections), I (infected and infectious, with symptoms), R (recovered, immune, and non-infectious), or D…
